events.headline: Axsome prices $174 million public offering of common stock
events.detail: Axsome priced an underwritten public offering of 2,000,000 shares at $87.00 per share for gross proceeds of about $174 million, to fund ongoing clinical development of its late-stage candidates and general corporate purposes.

source.title: Axsome Therapeutics Announces Pricing of Public Offering of $174 Million of Shares of Common Stock

events.headline: AXS-07 meets co-primary endpoints in Phase 3 MOMENTUM migraine trial
events.detail: In patients with a history of inadequate response to prior acute migraine treatment, AXS-07 achieved statistically significant pain freedom (19.9% vs 6.7% placebo, p<0.001) and freedom from most bothersome symptom (36.9% vs 24.4%, p=0.002) at 2 hours, and outperformed active comparator rizatriptan on a key secondary endpoint.

source.title: Axsome Therapeutics Announces AXS-07 Achieves Co-Primary and Key Secondary Endpoints in MOMENTUM Phase 3 Migraine Trial in Patients with History of Inadequate Response

events.headline: AXS-05 misses the Week 6 primary endpoint against bupropion in the STRIDE-1 treatment-resistant depression trial
events.detail: AXS-05 showed a numerically greater MADRS reduction than active comparator bupropion at Week 6 (11.6 vs 9.4 points) but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.117); the company said key secondary endpoints, including earlier timepoints, were met, per its same-day press release (also opened).
events.source_quote: Shares of Axsome Therapeutics fell nearly 15% today after the company reported results for the STRIDE-1 phase 3 study.

source.title: Here's Why Axsome Therapeutics Fell as Much as 14.7% Today

events.opened_note: Company press release (GlobeNewswire, 2020-03-30, same trial data) also opened for the clinical facts; this article was used as the cited source because it explicitly links the price move to the trial result, which the press release does not do.

events.headline: AXS-07 meets both co-primary endpoints in Phase 3 INTERCEPT early-treatment migraine trial
events.detail: AXS-07 produced pain freedom in 32.6% vs 16.3% of placebo patients (p=0.002) and freedom from most bothersome symptom in 43.9% vs 26.7% (p=0.003) at 2 hours, and reduced progression of migraine pain and rescue-medication use versus placebo.

source.title: Axsome Therapeutics Announces AXS-07 Achieves Both Co-Primary Endpoints and Prevents Migraine Pain Progression in the INTERCEPT Phase 3 Trial in the Early Treatment of Migraine

events.headline: AXS-05 meets primary endpoint in ADVANCE-1 pivotal trial for Alzheimer's disease agitation
events.detail: In the Phase 2/3 ADVANCE-1 trial (366 patients), AXS-05 produced a statistically significant reduction in Cohen Mansfield Agitation Inventory score versus placebo (p=0.010), with improvement emerging by week 3 and 73% of patients meeting a clinical-response threshold versus 57% on placebo.

source.title: Axsome Therapeutics Announces AXS-05 Achieves Primary Endpoint in the ADVANCE-1 Pivotal Phase 2/3 Trial in Alzheimer's Disease Agitation

events.headline: Axsome's Q1 2020 filing flags COVID-19 as a business-disruption risk during its cluster of pivotal readouts
events.detail: Axsome's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2020 (filed May 11, 2020) listed 'unforeseen circumstances or other disruptions to normal business operations arising from or related to COVID-19' among risks to its forward-looking statements. Connection to this business: the pandemic's onset coincided with the market-wide selloff of March 2020 and with the company's cluster of Phase 3 readouts (STRIDE-1, INTERCEPT, ADVANCE-1) reported over the following weeks.

source.title: Axsome Therapeutics, Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2020

events.headline: FDA accepts AXS-05 New Drug Application for major depressive disorder and grants Priority Review
events.detail: The FDA accepted for filing Axsome's NDA for AXS-05 in MDD, based on the GEMINI and ASCEND trials, and granted Priority Review, setting a PDUFA target action date of August 22, 2021.

source.title: Axsome Therapeutics Announces FDA Acceptance and Priority Review of New Drug Application for AXS-05 for Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder

events.headline: Axsome discloses FDA letter citing unspecified deficiencies in the AXS-05 MDD NDA; shares fall sharply
events.detail: In its Q2 2021 results, Axsome disclosed that on July 30, 2021 the FDA notified it of deficiencies that precluded discussion of labeling and post-marketing requirements at that time, without stating what the deficiencies were; the company said the notification did not reflect a final review decision.
events.source_quote: Shares of Axsome Therapeutics are down 14% ... after a brutal sell-off on Aug. 9 wiped out nearly 50% of its equity value.

source.title: Why Axsome Therapeutics Is Plunging Again Today

events.opened_note: Company Q2 2021 earnings release (GlobeNewswire, 2021-08-09) also opened for the FDA-letter facts; this article was cited because it makes the explicit link between the disclosure and the same-day/next-day price move, which the earnings release does not address. Price figures are the article's own and are not independently verified here.

events.headline: FDA review of AXS-05 MDD application misses its PDUFA target date; agency requests no new data
events.detail: Axsome said the FDA informed it on August 20, 2021 that the NDA review would not be completed by the August 22, 2021 PDUFA target action date, but that the FDA had not requested additional information and the review remained ongoing.

source.title: Axsome Therapeutics Provides Update on the New Drug Application for AXS-05 for the Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder

events.headline: FDA approves Auvelity (AXS-05) for major depressive disorder in adults
events.detail: The FDA approved Auvelity (dextromethorphan HBr and bupropion HCl extended-release tablets) as, per the company, the first rapid-acting oral medicine approved for MDD with labeling citing statistically significant antidepressant efficacy versus placebo starting at one week, and the first new oral mechanism of action approved for MDD in over 60 years.

source.title: Axsome Therapeutics Announces FDA Approval of AUVELITY (dextromethorphan HBr and bupropion HCl) for the Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder in Adults
source.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (EDGAR, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

events.headline: Axsome announces U.S. commercial availability of Auvelity
events.detail: Axsome announced that Auvelity became available by prescription in the United States for MDD in adults, roughly two months after FDA approval.

source.title: Axsome Therapeutics Announces Availability of AUVELITY, the First and Only Oral NMDA Receptor Antagonist for the Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder in Adults

events.headline: Axsome reports full-year 2024 net product revenue of $385.7 million while still posting a net loss
events.detail: For full-year 2024, Axsome reported total net product revenue of $385.7 million (Auvelity $291.4 million, Sunosi $94.3 million), up sharply from 2023, alongside a net loss of $287.2 million for the year, versus a $239.2 million net loss in 2023.

source.title: Axsome Therapeutics Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2024 Financial Results and Provides Business Update

horizon_notes.1: In the year following the cutoff, the pre-cutoff catalyst calendar largely played out: AXS-07 posted two more positive migraine readouts (MOMENTUM [e2], INTERCEPT [e4]) and AXS-05 posted a mixed record, meeting its primary endpoint in Alzheimer's-disease agitation (ADVANCE-1 [e5]) but missing the Week 6 primary endpoint against an active comparator in treatment-resistant depression (STRIDE-1 [e3]). The company had not yet filed, let alone had accepted, an NDA for AXS-05 in MDD by the one-year anniversary, and it raised $174 million in a public offering within days of cutoff [e1], addressing the funding-runway question the pre-cutoff packet had flagged as unresolved. Interpretation: the packet listed five pending readouts as open catalysts and flagged cash runway as a specific risk; a reader who expected all five readouts to replicate GEMINI's success would have been wrong about STRIDE-1, while the packet gave no indication the company would resolve its cash question via a large follow-on offering within two days.
horizon_notes.3: By the third anniversary, AXS-05's MDD program had gone from NDA acceptance under Priority Review [e7], through an FDA-disclosed deficiency letter that coincided with a sharp reported share-price move [e8] and a missed PDUFA target date [e9], to FDA approval as Auvelity in August 2022 [e10] and U.S. commercial launch two months later [e11]. The pivotal GEMINI/ASCEND package the pre-cutoff packet was built around had by then converted into an approved, marketed product, roughly two years later than the fourth-quarter-2020 NDA filing target implied by the company's own late-2019 catalyst list. Interpretation: the pre-cutoff packet's as_of_facts and catalysts said nothing about manufacturing or analytical-methods review risk; the delay that actually occurred in 2021 came from a category of regulatory risk (chemistry, manufacturing and controls) that was not named as a specific risk in the packet.
horizon_notes.5: By the fifth anniversary, Axsome had also brought a second commercial product (Sunosi) into its revenue base and reported full-year 2024 net product revenue of $385.7 million, up sharply from 2023, while still recording a net loss for the year [e12]. The company had moved from a pre-revenue, single-asset-dependent clinical-stage profile at cutoff to a multi-product commercial company, though profitability had not followed revenue growth by this anniversary. Interpretation: the pre-cutoff packet's central open question -- whether a second confirming pivotal trial in a company with no approved products justified a position given regulatory and commercial risk -- was resolved directionally toward commercial approval and launch, but only after both a failed confirmatory trial (STRIDE-1) and a manufacturing-related regulatory delay that the packet's catalysts list did not foreshadow.

aftermath.attribution_caveat: Price moves have many causes; the events here are what was public, not a proof of why the price moved.
gaps: The exact date Axsome submitted the AXS-05 MDD NDA to the FDA was not independently confirmed by a primary source opened in this research; a December 1, 2020 company release said the NDA was 'on track for submission in January 2021,' and FDA acceptance with Priority Review followed on April 26, 2021.

The CONCERT Phase 2 narcolepsy readout (AXS-12), listed as an upcoming catalyst in player.json as of the November 2019 Q3 update, was actually announced December 3, 2019 -- before this case's cutoff (December 17, 2019) -- so it is out of scope for this post-cutoff timeline and is not included as an event.

The 2022 Sunosi (solriamfetol) licensing/acquisition from Jazz Pharmaceuticals, which contributed to the FY2024 revenue reported in [e12], was not independently researched for its own date, terms or consideration in this pass.

The May 2022 securities class action concerning AXS-07 (migraine) chemistry-manufacturing-controls disclosures was identified in secondary sources but not included as an event: it concerns AXS-07, not the AXS-05 MDD program the pre-cutoff packet centered on, and was outside this case's event budget.

A second macro event on 2022 interest-rate increases and biotech financing conditions was considered but not included, to keep the macro-event count low relative to company-specific events; only the COVID-19 disclosure [e6] is included.

scene_check.voice: Their depression drug just hit the main target in its second pivotal trial, and the FDA already gave it breakthrough status. They say that's enough to file next year. I think this is their moment.

claims.text: second positive well-controlled trial in MDD
the company says the package supports an NDA filing in the second half of 2020

debrief_check.s1: True as stated, and the pattern did not simply repeat: within the year AXS-05 met its endpoint in Alzheimer's agitation but missed against an active comparator in treatment-resistant depression [e3][e5].
debrief_check.s2: True. Designation did not shorten the road: the NDA was accepted with priority review in April 2021, then hit a deficiency letter over manufacturing and analytical methods and missed its target date, before approval as Auvelity in August 2022 [e7][e8][e9][e10].
debrief_check.s3: The company did not file within the year; the filing came about a year later than the friend's 'next year'. It also sold $174 million of stock three days after the cutoff, which answered the cash question the packet had flagged, at the cost of dilution [e1].

assumptions.text: The regulator will accept two trials as enough to approve the drug.
The other four readouts will go the same way as this one.
The company can raise the cash it needs without wrecking the price.
After a 25x run the price already assumes approval; the risk is down.
I don't have enough evidence to take a position either way.

thesis_check.a1: Evidence: the filing came in early 2021, later than the guided second half of 2020; the regulator accepted it with priority review, then sent a deficiency letter over manufacturing and analytical questions, missed its target date, and approved the drug in August 2022 [e7][e8][e9][e10]. For this assumption: right in the end, and outside a one-year horizon. Unknown: how much of the delay a reader could have priced in 2019; the packet did not name manufacturing risk.
thesis_check.a2: Evidence: the migraine drug won both its trials and the depression drug won in Alzheimer's agitation, but missed against an active comparator in treatment-resistant depression in March 2020 [e2][e3][e4][e5]. For this assumption: three of four, and the miss came in the same drug. Unknown: which readouts the market weighted most; the record does not attribute moves.
thesis_check.a3: Evidence: the company sold $174 million of stock three days after the cutoff [e1]. For this assumption: supported; the funding question was answered within the week, at the cost of dilution. Unknown: the price paid by earlier holders is in the result tiles, not in the record of events.
thesis_check.a4: Evidence: within the year came a big equity raise, one failed trial, three successful ones and a pandemic [e1][e3][e4][e5][e6]; see the result tiles for what the price did over your horizon. For this assumption: the price did not fall apart, nor did it run further inside the year. Unknown: the drug's later approval and launch lie beyond one year [e10][e11].
thesis_check.a5: Evidence: a year of mixed readouts and a raise, with the decisive regulatory events two years away [e1][e3][e7]. For this assumption: fair; the packet listed the catalysts but could not rank them. Unknown: whether waiting for the filing would have been cheaper; the tiles say.

walkthrough.stage_text: Three days in, the company sells $174 million of new stock. The runway question in the packet is answered; existing holders own less of the company.

event.detail: AXS-05 showed a numerically greater MADRS reduction than active comparator bupropion at Week 6 (11.6 vs 9.4 points) but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.117); the company said key secondary endpoints, including earlier timepoints, were met, per its same-day press release (also opened).

walkthrough.stage_text: Four months in, the drug meets its primary endpoint in Alzheimer's agitation and the migraine drug wins its second trial. Three of four readouts have gone the company's way; the filing in depression is still ahead, and a pandemic has begun.

walkthrough.stage_text: Twenty months in, after the filing was accepted with priority review, the company discloses a regulator's letter citing deficiencies in the application. What the deficiencies are is not public; the decision date is two weeks away.

baseline.narrative: Your window ends before the first new development covered by this story. The starting record leaves the regulatory, trial and financing questions open.

checks.a1: Unresolved. The starting record shows only the company's own view that its two pivotal trials support filing; no regulatory response has yet occurred to test that.
checks.a2: Unresolved. Four more trial readouts were still pending at cutoff, so this record cannot say whether the first positive result will repeat.
checks.a3: Unresolved. A stated plan not to raise new equity before readouts does not establish how any future financing, if needed, would affect the price.
checks.a4: Unresolved. A share price level cannot by itself establish how much of a possible future approval is already reflected in it.
checks.a5: Choosing not to take a position is consistent with uncertainty. This outcome alone cannot tell us whether waiting was the better decision.

updates.narrative: Three days into the window, the company priced a $174 million stock offering to fund its late-stage programs.

checks.a3: Partly supported. The company raised $174 million in a dilutive stock offering three days after cutoff, resolving the near-term funding question it had flagged. This record does not show how the offering price compared to prior trading levels.

updates.narrative: Ten days later, the first of the four pending readouts arrived: a migraine trial met both of its co-primary endpoints.

checks.a2: Partly supported. The first of four pending readouts, a migraine trial, met both co-primary endpoints against placebo. One result on its own cannot show whether the remaining three will follow the same pattern.

updates.narrative: Three months in, a depression trial against an active comparator missed its primary endpoint, while the first migraine trial had already succeeded.

checks.a2: Mixed. The second readout, a depression trial against an active comparator, missed statistical significance on its primary endpoint, though the company reported secondary endpoints were met. Not every readout is repeating the first result.

updates.narrative: Within a month, a second migraine trial met both co-primary endpoints and a separate trial in Alzheimer's-related agitation met its primary endpoint. All four pending readouts have now reported, split three-to-one in the company's favor.

checks.a2: Partly supported. Three of the four pending readouts met their primary endpoints (two migraine trials, one Alzheimer's-agitation trial); one depression trial missed significance. The readout cycle did not repeat cleanly, but was not a broad failure either.

updates.narrative: About sixteen months later, the regulator accepted the depression drug's application for filing and granted Priority Review.

checks.a1: Partly supported. The regulator accepted the application built on the two pivotal trials for review and granted Priority Review, a step beyond the company's own view that they were sufficient. Acceptance for review is not an approval decision.

updates.narrative: The regulator then disclosed unspecified deficiencies in the application and, two weeks later, missed its own target decision date without requesting new data.

checks.a1: Mixed. The regulator disclosed unspecified deficiencies and later missed its target decision date, without requesting additional data or issuing a rejection. This record does not show whether the two pivotal trials themselves were in question.

updates.narrative: About two and a half years after cutoff, the regulator approved the drug for major depressive disorder.

checks.a1: Supported. The regulator approved the drug based on its original two pivotal trials, after the earlier deficiency letter and missed target date. The trials did ultimately support approval, though not on the original timeline.

updates.narrative: Two months after approval, the drug became commercially available in the United States, converting the company from a clinical-stage developer awaiting its first approval into one with a marketed product.
